messages:
maria: Quick follow-up from the console RFC meeting earlier — observed cold-start latency spikes when users open dashboards after deploys. Root cause seems to be query-layer warmups + RBAC checks happening synchronously. Want to decide tradeoffs for 2 approaches: eager warmup with cached authz vs lazy authz per query.

sam: Can you paste the perf numbers?

maria: Sure — 95th latency for first page load jumped from 350ms -> ~1.8s during busy deploys. Warmup accounted for ~1.1s (batching + model loading), RBAC checks added 250-400ms per tenant because we do N role checks per panel/widget.

jin: Oof. That's quite visible. What's current RBAC flow? Inline calls to authz-service for each panel/widget?

maria: Yes. Pseudocode:
```
for panel in panels:
  allowed = authz.check(user, panel.resource)
  if allowed: run query(panel)
```
This runs several authz RPCs per page.

omar: Two obvious levers: 1) pre-compute tenant->view bitmask (single call per page), 2) cache authz results in local LRU with short TTL + invalidation on role change.

leo: Also consider combining warmup with authz warm cache: background prefetcher that calls authz once then warms query engines. Tradeoff: risk showing slightly stale data if role changes right after prefetch.

sam: What's our SLAs on showing updated permissions? Enterprise requires changes to take effect within 1 minute, right?

jin: Yes, 60s is typical for our support contracts.

maria: So stale window must be <= 60s. We can use event-driven invalidation: auth service emits role-change event to kafka -> console listens and evicts cache keys for tenant.

omar: Implementation complexity: event plumbing + sequencing, plus more bursty invalidations during org churn. But seems feasible.

leo: If we go with single-call per page (bitmask), we can reduce RPCs by 5-10x and reduce latency. Memory cost is small (bitmask per user-session). TTL 30s + event invalidate meets 60s SLA.

sam: Any security concerns? Need to ensure bitmask is signed if cached client-side. But if server-side only, OK.

maria: Plan proposal:
  - short-term (canary next week): add per-page authz aggregator that calls authz once and caches result TTL=30s. Add metrics.
  - mid-term: implement kafka invalidation + prefetcher that warms query layer & authz in background during deploys.
  - long-term: refactor query executor to accept permission filters so we can push authz into query planner to reduce panel-level gates.

jin: LGTM. For canary, I'll own the aggregator and add metrics panels for warmup_hits, authz_rpc_count_per_page, first_load_p95.

omar: I can wire event topic and help with consumer + eviction logic.

leo: I'll write the small RFC update and include rollout checklist (feature flag + canary to 5% orgs).

auth-bot: deploy check passed for branch console-auth-aggregator. CI: 4/4 green :white_check_mark:

maria: Thanks all — scheduling 30m follow-up Wed to review metrics post-canary. If anyone has objections to the plan, flag here.

sam: No objections. :+1:

jin: No objections.

omar: Fine with me.

leo: Ack.
